mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 10% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment may decline.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate exceeds 10% but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth is positive and the unemployment rate decreases, it indicates a strong economy, leading to higher S&P 500 returns as corporate performance improves.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive and unemployment decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates encourage borrowing and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as access to cheap capital increases.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is below 1% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the 20-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production suggests higher economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as supply chains and manufacturing strengthen.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rapid growth in retail sales indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as companies experience increased revenues.
failure_condition: If retail sales growth exceeds 10% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates alongside falling unemployment may signal tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of the 5-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 50% of the time.
